text:
joel: FYI partner reported duplicate side-effects when a 429 hit as our SDK started token refresh. attached minimal log shows immediate retry + queued drain -> two applies.

priya: can you paste redacted logs? sounds like a refresh vs retry race.

joel: snippet:
```
2025-06-10T10:02:01Z req id=a1 status=429
2025-06-10T10:02:01Z auth refresh start
2025-06-10T10:02:01Z internal retry -> 200 (applied)
2025-06-10T10:02:02Z auth refresh done; drained queue -> 200 (applied)
```

amy: clear double-apply. Proposals: default to queueing mutates while refresh in-flight (hold), add optional client-side fingerprint dedupe TTL=10s, and make sampleapp set Idempotency-Key by default.

kevin: parity: Node/JS and Python differ today. Align default to "hold" on both SDKs and expose `replay_strategy` config to allow passthrough.

priya: also respect Retry-After header; if present and >900ms treat as authoritative. For missing header use jittered backoff: delay = base * (1.5 ** attempt) * (0.7 + rand()*0.6), cap 2500ms.

amy: tests: add deterministic e2e mocking 429->refresh race and assert only 1 applied side-effect when hold + idempotency enabled. Add telemetry metric sdk.replay.during_refresh.count.

ci-bot: CI queued: run/tests (node-sdk) #3101 by kevin

joel: timeline: small patch for Node this sprint, Py follow-up next. I'll file partner note and RFC link here.

priya: add code comments in both SDKs explaining the hold tradeoffs to avoid regressions. Thanks all.
